`ReferenceProseFidelityCheck.reportUnfaithfulReferenceProse` — the production predicate, never a
re-expression of it — with the records named in the second column served to it as the answer's cited
list, off a chart the real injector built. Serving them, rather than letting each answer's own
citation markers select them, is what makes that column a variable; the capture's markers therefore
play no part in the table. The four rows the two cases below pin are driven through
`LlmInferenceService.search` instead, where `extractCitedReferences` selects from the markers, and
agree. The first two rows are this issue's captured answer, all six clauses word for word from the
issue body. The remaining rows are its opening clause, and the record's own sentence, against a
two-row verbatim slice that renders the same finding byte for byte, so that one substitution at a
time can be undone. *Reported* names the citation the check
stated; every other row is an empty list, which is a measurement of none rather than the absence of
one.

| answer | records served | reported |
|---|---|---|
| the capture, six clauses | its thirteen findings | — |
| the capture, six clauses | every reference record | — |
| its opening clause, both defects | that finding | — |
| its opening clause, repetition collapsed, allergen still short | that finding | that finding |
| its opening clause, allergen in full, repetition kept | that finding | — |
| its opening clause, both repaired, the capture's gloss kept | that finding | that finding |
| its opening clause, both repaired, gloss dropped | that finding | — |
| the record's own sentence reproduced to its end | that finding | — |
| the same, allergen a letter short | that finding | that finding |

Three readings. Each rests on a difference between rows; where one states which GATE a row declined
at, or how long the runs were, that is a second measurement over the same answers and is named as one.

- **The check is silent on the captured answer.** Defect 1 is why, not defect 2: it sits inside the
  same sentence and cuts the answer's agreement with that finding into runs the floor rejects. Lower
  `MIN_REPRODUCED_WORDS` to eight and the answer is reported, its WARN naming a run of eight words;
  lower it to seven and a second WARN names the run the truncated allergen ends, of seven. This is the
  residue Decision 61 records as *"A substitution inside a reproduction shorter than twelve words,
  wherever it sits"*, met by a second defect of the same sentence rather than by a short answer. Which
  silence it is differs between the first row and the third, and both are silences: on all six clauses
  the check compares and finds no divergence, its sixth clause having reproduced one other finding's
  record to the floor — the duplicate-therapy finding about active order Dexamethasone, and that one
  alone of the eighteen reference records the chart carries; on
  the opening clause alone nothing reaches the floor and it declines before comparing.
  **And the defect this silence rests on did not reproduce when the issue was re-measured after
  Decision 59's own rules shipped.** They went in with
  [#343](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-chartsearchai/pull/343), and this issue's follow-up
  comment re-measured the same patient and question on `main` @ `3b98b04e` across three byte-identical
  runs: each parenthetical carries one code there, so defect 1 did not reproduce — nor did defect 2 on
  that chart, though the same comment records the same class of truncation on another one, which the
  third reading below is about. The mechanism recorded here is therefore a reading of THIS capture, in
  which two defects co-occur, and not a standing property of what a current head answers. What no
  capture supplies is defect 2 standing alone inside a long enough reproduction; that is row four,
  built rather than captured.
- **A report is not evidence that a drug name was mangled.** Row six spells the allergen correctly and
  is reported all the same, for the gloss that follows it — drop that and it goes silent, which is
  row seven. Row four is reported for the shortened allergen instead, and drops the gloss without
  going quiet: its WARN is the same fourteen words either way. The two rows share a verdict and not a
  cause, which is the whole of what a report tells a reader.
- **Where the answer reproduces the record's sentence to its own end, the name is what the report
  turns on.** The last two rows differ in one letter. The cross-reactivity-group sentence the issue's
  follow-up comment captured on a second chart (`Ibuprof` for `Ibuprofen`) is that shape; that answer
  is quoted with an ellipsis, so what the check would have said about it is not something this
  repository can settle.

**What is pinned.** `ReferenceProseFidelityTest.theCapturedAnswerOfIssue338IsBelowTheFloorAndTheSameSentenceWithoutItsRepetitionIsReported`
holds rows three and four, the gate it declined at and the empty
`unfaithfullyRenderedCitations` the decline publishes;
`.aTruncatedDrugNameDecidesTheReportWhereTheRestOfTheReproductionIsFaithful` holds the last two. Each
says at its own site what it does and does not discriminate. The other five rows are measurements with
no case behind them. Both cases read the verbatim slice rather than the shipped knowledge base,
because a case reading rendered TEXT is what `DrugReferenceTestSupport.shippedEntries()` reserves a
slice for, and `SlicedReferenceRowProvenanceTest` is what holds that slice to the dataset field for
field. Raising the floor far enough reddens both; the values either side of twelve are pre-existing
cases' to hold, and do.

**And the empty list reaches a client.** A decline states `[]` on Decision 74's
`unfaithfullyRenderedCitations` — which the README's contract for that key already says is not a
certificate of faithfulness, and rows one and two are the answer that shows why. Note beside the
first reading that this decision's own rule 1 DOES see the captured answer, for its repeated code —
but only in the log: `ClassCodeFidelityCheck` publishes nothing, so the response states nothing about
either defect.

**One candidate this does not refuse, named because a section called "Re-measured" is where it
belongs.** The drug-name rule the bullet above refutes is UNALIGNED — *"any answer token that is a
proper prefix of a name a cited record states"* — and alignment is a different predicate: inside a
reproduction this check has already established, the question becomes whether the answer's word is a
proper prefix of the record's word AT THAT POSITION. That removes the hits arising between an answer
word and a name some cited record states elsewhere: the module's own
`Ethinylestradiol (ethinyl estradiol)` label is word-identical at every position of a faithful
reproduction, and the pairs the bullet counts are pairs of NAMES rather than of aligned positions.
**What it does not remove is a correct answer normalising a spelling the record carries.** A
`safety_finding` embeds this patient's own prescription display, so a record can carry `Amoxicilline`
at the position where a correct answer writes the INN `Amoxicillin` — one of the 67 localized
spellings `matchesOrderName`'s javadoc counts in the 3.7.1 demo dictionary — and a spelling variant of
one substance, `terazosine` against `terazosin`, reaches the same position the same way. So alignment
narrows the rule; it does not answer it. Nor would such a rule buy anything at the current floor,
where a substitution inside a long enough reproduction is already reported; its whole value would be a
floor lowered for that class alone, which Decision 61 is canonical for and does not by itself refuse.
What it would have to get past is its own false-positive measurement and Decision 35's standing bar
that a check which cries wolf is worse than no check. **A corpus to take that measurement over
exists in this repository — thin, and labelled for a different question, rather than absent.** The
captures under `eval/drift-metric/fixtures` carry each answer's `safetyWarnings` beside its
citations, and a chip's `drug` and `detail` are two of the operands
`DrugReferenceInjector.renderFinding` composes a `safety_finding` record from, so that record's own
detail SENTENCE — where an answer's reproduction of a finding sits — is reconstructible from a
capture word for word, even though no capture's citation object carries a word of the record's own
text. Measured 2026-09-04 from a throwaway harness driving `reportUnfaithfulReferenceProse` itself
(never a re-expression of it) over all 72 json files, each capture's reconstructed chips served as
its own cited records: of the 42 captured answers 27 carry chips, 16 reproduce a reconstructed
record to the floor — the population a rule scoped inside an established reproduction could fire in
at this floor — and the check states a citation on 9 of them. Those nine are THIS check's reports
and not a candidate rule's false alarms; what the sixteen give a candidate is somewhere to be run.
Two things that corpus does not carry, and both are why it is thin rather than why it would be
unavailable: a label saying whether a report on a capture is a TRUE one; and any `drug_reference`
record's text at all, no capture carrying it — the reconstruction reaches a `safety_finding`'s
detail, and what `renderFinding` appends after it is approximated. **What it does carry is a
per-file provenance record, and it has to be READ rather than characterised from the shape of the
tree** — an earlier draft of this paragraph characterised the whole of it as the drift metric's own
perturbed answers, which its own `eval/drift-metric/fixtures/probe-safety/PROVENANCE.md` refuses in
as many words: *"Everything not marked **CONSTRUCTED** or **COUNTERFACTUAL** below is a verbatim
live capture — the markers are the record"*. Those markers answer a different question from this one
— whether an ANSWER was constructed to give the drift SCORER a failure to catch, not whether it
renders a cited record faithfully — which is why the label this measurement wants is still missing.
What they do settle is which captures are the module's own output. The nine reported files are FOUR
distinct answers — two of them live captures, the other two single-token edits of one of those,
`Major` for `Moderate` and for `Minor` (measured on this head by hashing the nine files and their
nine `answer` fields). `shipped-clean/agnes__safety-warfarin.json` (*"byte-identical"*) is one of
the two, and four other arms carry that file unedited because each changes one other cell — five of
the nine are one live answer. The second is `severity-overstated/steven__safety-rifabutin.json` (*"A
**live capture**, verbatim and unedited"*). On both, the divergence is between the captured answer
and the chip text the same file carries, and is legible without running anything: the answer writes
`plateet` where the chip writes `platelet`, and `CYP402C8` where the chip writes `CYP450 2C8`. So
this check's reports on the live subset are true divergences and not wolf-crying — which matters
because `shipped-clean/`'s own contract is *"Nothing here may be flagged; if it is, the guards are
crying wolf on the answers the module actually produces"*, a contract over the drift scorer's guards
and not over this check, and the closest thing in the tree to the label above. What stays thin is
the BREADTH: those nine reports are four answers about two patients, and the sixteen that reach the
floor add one more patient. The live corpus Decision 35 used is outside this repository.

What this leaves is the bullet above, unchanged: defect 2 is open, and a remedy still has that
bullet's measurement to get past. It is recorded here because *"the prose check covers it now"* is the
reading a maintainer arrives at from Decisions 61 and 74 alone, and the capture this issue is about is
one the check is silent on.

### Trade-offs

- **+** Two of #338's four defects become visible to a maintainer from logs alone, deterministically, with no model call and no wire or UI change.
- **+** Detection lands before any remedy, which is the order this module's own probe harness argues for: a remedy gated by an A/B in which no metric reproduces the defect *"ships either ungated or judged ineffective, on a harness that structurally cannot see it"* (`eval/drift-metric/capture_probe_safety.sh`).
- **−** Nothing a clinician reads changes. The malformed answer in #338 is still malformed.
- **−** The false-alarm rate is unmeasured against live answers, for the reason above. The first deployment that logs these lines is also the first measurement of them.
- **−** The rules are gated behind Decision 35's own three gates, so an answer that states a repeated code while citing no code-bearing record is silent. That is the same conservatism, inherited rather than re-argued, and it is a place a real defect can hide.
- **−** A third question about brackets now lives in this class, and the two patterns it reads are still not allowed to merge. The structural guard is what keeps that from decaying into a private matcher.
---

## Decision 60: A bounded pairwise interaction list states its own bounds on the response

**Status: Accepted** (August 2026) — implemented, issue [#336](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-chartsearchai/issues/336).

### Context

`chartsearchai.drugSafety.maxPairChips` truncates both pairwise interaction arms, and until this change it stated that fact only to a server-side `WARN`. Measured on the 3.7.1 standalone against the bundled DDInter knowledge base, stock GPs, patient `dc8560c9` on eight anti-inflammatories: the screening arm found **18** above-floor pairs, reported **10**, and the `/search` response carried no trace of the other eight — the answer text ended in an ordinary enumeration, the chip array simply stopped, and every `references[].withheldInteractions` read `0` (that field is a different concept, the partners one cited record does not show). A clinician asking to have a medication list screened and receiving ten chips was handed a list that reads as exhaustive.

`maxPairChips()`'s own javadoc recorded this as a settled trade — *"a clinician-facing '10 of 72 shown' needs a per-question container the chip API does not have (chips are per-drug findings), so it is a frontend change rather than a module one"* — and `config.xml` said the WARN was *"currently the only place the withheld count appears"*. **That premise is half right and its conclusion was wrong.** The chip ARRAY has no per-question container; the RESPONSE is one. `safetyWarnings` is a key of a per-question map, and a key beside it is a module change, not a frontend one. #131 closed on making the cap a global property, which decided who chooses the number and left the truncation invisible for whoever reads one particular answer.

### Decision

**Both pairwise arms state how many pairs they found beside how many they reported, and that statement travels to every surface that carries chips.**

- **`PairChipExtent`** — an immutable `{found, reported}` produced by the arms, carried on `ChartAnswer.getPairChipExtent()`, published as `interactionPairs` on the `/search` response and on the `done` and `grounded` SSE events. `found` is the candidate count before the cut; `reported` is what the cut left, i.e. `min(found, maxPairChips())`, read off the cut and never off the GP.
- **Both arms, one statement.** Their gates are mutually exclusive (the question-pair arm needs two or more question-named reference drugs, the screen needs none), so at most one runs per question and one field speaks for both — the same argument #131 uses for the two arms sharing one cap. Publishing it for only the arm the ticket measured would have left it silently absent on exactly the question shape the other answers. **Two arms turned out not to be enough, and Decision 65 (issue [#356](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-chartsearchai/issues/356)) is the residue**: between them those two gates exclude the single-drug prescribing question, where the drug-in-play arm does the screening and stated nothing — so the field was silently absent on the commonest drug-safety question there is. Read that decision beside this one; it amends this bullet, the `PairChipExtent` bullet's `reported` definition above (`min(found, maxPairChips())` is the two capped arms' rule and not the third's), the "at most one record per pass" rule, and the trade-off below about `reported` counting pairs.
- **A caller-supplied sink, not a field.** `validate`'s widest arity gains a nullable `PairChipExtent.Sink`; `LlmInferenceService` creates one per call. `DrugSafetyValidator` is a Spring singleton, so a field would be one slot shared by every concurrent request — #172's constraint, met by the shape rather than by discipline, exactly as Decision 58 met it for `resolvedOrderEntries`.
- **The counts, and deliberately not the list.** Which pairs went and at what ratings stays in the `WARN`. Putting the withheld pairs on the wire is the unbounded, question-controlled expansion the cap exists to prevent (72 chips carrying 42,708 characters, `maxPairChips()`'s own measurement).
- **Zero is a measurement and absence is not.** An arm that ran and related no pairs states `found == 0` — a complete screen, positively assertable. **Decisions 69 and 71 amend this bullet**: an arm can also relate pairs and be left with none of its own by a cede to another arm, and both pairwise arms now state nothing there rather than a zero — the question-pair arm's nothing being consumed by Decision 65's fallback, the screening arm's reaching the client. `null` says the producer stated nothing. What that covers is carried by `PairChipExtent`'s class javadoc and by `README.md`'s client-facing form, the second because it is the only one a frontend author reads; this decision points at them rather than restating it, which is the discipline `getOrderActive()`'s own list prescribes. **What it deliberately does not do is count them**, and that is the part worth recording: three drafts of these bullets published a count and each was refuted by the next review — three situations where the class listed two, one home while README held a second, and two situations while the async early-`done` answer was a third nobody had counted. After a second refuted attempt the move is to stop making a claim of that kind, not to make a better one.
- **Published once, on `validate`'s normal return, from a local both arms assign** — never per arm. The public entry answers a `RuntimeException` with an empty warning list, so a sink written as each arm finished could describe a screen whose chips were then discarded. Not test-observable, because no reachable path throws between an arm and the return; recorded here because nothing else can record it.

### Rejected alternatives

- **A synthetic "the screen was bounded" chip**, which the ticket offers as one of its two suggestions. A `SafetyWarning` is a finding about a drug: it would reach the prompt through `DrugReferenceInjector.renderFinding` — the pairwise gates are on the QUESTION alone, so both arms are live in the pre-answer pass — where `strengthClause` would give it neither of the two clauses every injected finding states, the empty default `CLAUDE.md` calls *"a defect waiting on a caller"*. It would also break `SafetyWarning.getType()`'s documented three values, which clients render on. A statement about a list is not a member of it.
- **Publishing `withheld` — as a third wire key, or as a Java accessor beside the two counts.** It is `found - reported`, and the two counts are what a client renders. A derived figure published beside a measured one is the shape #261 exists to stop, one level down, and the rule is taken on BOTH surfaces rather than on the wire alone: a first draft kept `getWithheld()` and `isBounded()` on the type, which no production code called and which made the ADR's own rule read as a wire-only exception.
- **An audit column.** `search_mode` and the reference slice each earned one; this is a wire contract, and no ticket asks to reconstruct capping after the fact. It can be added on evidence later.
- **Making the answer text say it.** A prompt clause is measurable only against the eval gate (#107's four arms), and the module's own rule is that a clinician-facing assertion about what the module withheld is not something the LLM should be asked to paraphrase.

### Trade-offs

- **+** The invariant the ticket asks for holds at every emission surface, and it holds for a surface nobody has written yet: `putSafetyChips` writes both keys, and `ChartSearchAiInteractionPairExtentTest` fails the build on a second write of the `safetyWarnings` KEY. Measured — a fourth site bypassing the helper, whether it calls the shared serializer or inlines the loop, reddens the structural case and the `done`-event case together; the key assertion is what reaches the inlined form, and the helper-name assertion alone does not.
- **+** A complete screen can now SAY it is complete. A truncation-only marker would have left completeness inferable only from the absence of a signal, which is the fail-open shape `getReferenceSlice()`'s "null is not zero" rule already refuses.
- **−** `reported` is a count of PAIRS and not of interaction chips. `addInteractionWarnings` raises interaction chips per drug in play and appends them to the same list, so a response can carry more of them than this states pairs. Named in the type's javadoc, in `README` and in the wire helper's, because a client rendering "10 of 18" off the chip count would publish a ratio of two populations. Nothing enforces it.
- **−** The widest `validate` arity now takes six parameters, and the five-argument seam above it wraps identically — so the two structural needles that delimit its body must spell all THREE lines of the declaration where two used to do. Both needles and both of their javadocs moved with it, as their own text prescribes.
- **−** `PairChipExtent.Sink.record` is public, so a caller other than the arms could state an extent. It is public for the same reason the `List<SafetyWarning> warnings` accumulator one level up is a plain public list — the sink belongs to the caller — and production has one writer, `DrugSafetyValidator.recordPairExtent`. Nothing structural enforces that; a second producer would be #151's two-derivations-that-agree shape.
- **−** Rendering "10 of 18 shown" is still a change in `openmrs-esm-chartsearchai`. This makes the fact available; it does not put it in front of a clinician. The ticket asks for the former ("something the client can render"), and the module cannot do the latter.
- **−** **The PROMPT's pairwise list is still silently bounded, and that is the ticket's own defect one channel over.** `DrugReferenceInjector.preAnswerFindings` takes the sinkless seam, so the pre-answer pass runs both arms under the same cut and injects only the survivors as citable `safety_finding` records — the model is handed 10 of 18 with nothing saying so, on the channel that shapes the prose a clinician reads first. Deferred rather than overlooked, and for a reason this repo can check: a clause added to the prompt is measurable only against the #107 eval gate, which four prior prompt levers failed, and the gate is a separate exercise from a wire contract. Recorded so the silence here is not read as coverage.

## Decision 61: Prose the answer reproduces from a cited reference record must be reproduced faithfully

**Issue [#337](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-chartsearchai/issues/337).** The safety validator produces a finding whose text is taken verbatim from the knowledge base, injects it as a citable `safety_finding`, and the model then rewrites it in the answer. Measured live on the 3.7.1 standalone, `main` @ `09717dc7`: the chip said *"Coadministration of local anesthetics with other oxidizing agents that **can also induce methemoglobinemia** such as antimalarials…"* and the answer, citing that finding, said *"…that **can also increase the risk**"*. The risk of what is absent, and methaemoglobinaemia — the entire content of that Major rating — reaches the clinician nowhere. A second capture deleted *"neuromuscular blockers, aminoglycoside antibiotics,"* from a botulinum toxin warning whose partner, neomycin, IS an aminoglycoside.

**The gap is a mechanism gap, and the docs asserted the mechanism existed.** A reference-group citation skips Tier-2 entailment entirely ([Decision 25](#decision-25-citation-grounding-tier-1-cosine--tier-2-entailment), #106/#122) and Tier-1 cosine barely moves when one phrase inside a long recitation changes. `ClassCodeFidelityCheck` ([Decision 35](#decision-35-a-class-code-in-the-answer-must-come-from-a-record-the-answer-cites)) compares one token shape and says nothing about prose. And this repository said, in `README.md`, in `CitationGroundingVerifier`'s javadoc AND in a line comment inside its demote-only branch, in `ChartSearchAiUtils`, and in [Decision 25](#decision-25-citation-grounding-tier-1-cosine--tier-2-entailment) and [Decision 41](#decision-41-a-composite-claims-negative-says-nothing-about-the-citation), that faithfulness of reference content was checked by the `DrugSafetyValidator` chips. The chips carry the true text but are a parallel list that nothing reconciles against the answer. Every hit found is corrected here. **This decision published a COUNT of them three times and every one was wrong** — five, then seven, then eight — and each was corrected by the next reviewer's sweep, so the count is gone rather than raised again. What defeated each sweep is the part worth keeping: the second missed Decision 25, spelled *"The faithfulness check for reference content is the deterministic safety validator"*, which contains none of the tokens it searched; the third missed a LINE COMMENT in `CitationGroundingVerifier`, because the enumeration said "in its javadoc" and the sweep scoped to javadoc. Sweep the CLAIM in several phrasings, over comments as well as docs, and read the hits.

### The decision

`ReferenceProseFidelityCheck` reports, at `WARN`, an answer that reproduces at least `MIN_REPRODUCED_WORDS` consecutive words of a record it cites whose `ChartSearchAiUtils.referenceGroup` is `REFERENCE_GROUP_REFERENCE`, and then — inside the sentence it was reproducing, on both sides — states different words. It runs on both answer paths beside the class-code check and never rewrites. It reached no wire field until [Decision 74](#decision-74-a-divergence-the-prose-check-finds-is-stated-on-the-response-not-only-in-the-log), which publishes the citations it warned about; every sentence below about what it REPORTS is unaffected by that.

SIX silencing legs keep it quiet, and every one is pinned by a case that reddens when the leg is removed — measured by mutation, not asserted, and named here so an auditor can check the pairing rather than trust the count:

| leg | the case that reddens when it is removed |
|---|---|
| the record ran out | `anAnswerThatReproducesTheRecordToItsLastWordIsNotReported` |
| the record's next word opens a new record sentence | `aFaithfulFullMechanismQuotationIsNotReported`, and `aRecordSentenceReproducedWholeAndFollowedByTheAnswersOwnIsNotReported` |
| the answer ran out | `anAnswerThatEndsTheSentenceWhereItStoppedCopyingIsNotReported` |
| the answer's next word opens a new answer sentence | `aQuotationTheAnswerClosedBeforeItsOwnNextSentenceIsNotReported`, `everyWayASentenceCanEndInTheSharedRuleEndsAnAnswerSentence` |
| another cited record ended innocently here (`Reproductions.explained`) | `aDivergenceAnotherCitedRecordEndsInnocentlyAtIsNotReported` |
| some reproduction carries on past here (`Reproductions.carriedThrough`) | `aDivergenceARecordsOwnReproductionCarriesThroughIsNotReported` |

**Eight of those cases exist only because three Phase 2 mutation sweeps found the leg unpinned, and two of them found a case pinning a leg other than the one it was named for.** Do not read the table as evidence the design was got right first time; read it as what the sweeps left. What each leg means:

- **the record ran out** (`anAnswerThatReproducesTheRecordToItsLastWordIsNotReported`), or **the record's next word opens a new sentence of the record** — the model reproduced a unit of the record faithfully and moved on. This is also what keeps the clauses `DrugReferenceInjector.renderFinding` appends out of the comparison at the seam: the detail goes through `DrugSafetyValidator.endSentence` whenever a clause follows, so `" This finding is a reason to withhold it."` always opens a new record sentence;
- **the answer ran out** (`anAnswerThatEndsTheSentenceWhereItStoppedCopyingIsNotReported`, which exits on this and not on the boundary bit), or **the answer's next word opens a new sentence of the answer** (`aQuotationTheAnswerClosedBeforeItsOwnNextSentenceIsNotReported`) — the model stopped copying rather than substituting;
- **another cited record explains the continuation.** Support is pooled across the cited records exactly as Decision 35 pools it for a class code, and here that is load-bearing rather than generous. One mechanism string is rendered into TWO records that are routinely cited together — `DrugSafetyValidator.buildInteractionWarning`'s detail and `DrugReferenceInjector`'s promoted interaction item, the same `getNote()` — and they lay it out differently: the finding ends the mechanism's sentence, while in the reference record it is one `"; "`-joined item of a list, so the next partner's name follows with no sentence boundary before it. Read against that record alone, an answer that reproduced the whole mechanism and welded a clause on looks exactly like a substitution. The live capture behind this issue cites both records in one sentence.

**Every maximal reproduction is its own candidate, not the longest.** An answer that substitutes inside a short run and then reproduces a long passage faithfully is the shape of the second capture; a longest-run reading would look at the faithful passage, find it innocent, and report nothing.

**The terminator set is spelled once, and the two questions over it are not interchangeable.** `ChartSearchAiUtils.SENTENCE_TERMINATORS` holds the set; `SENTENCE_BOUNDARY` is the SPLITTING question `CitationGroundingVerifier` cuts its claim units on, and `mayEndASentence` is the GAP question this check reads. Two spellings of one terminator set is the shape #260 records the cost of.

**The gap question is deliberately the WEAKER of the two, and that is a correction rather than a preference.** This change first asked `SENTENCE_BOUNDARY` of the gap, and published the argument that a boundary misread can only cost recall because both bit-driven conditions are silencing. That argument is sound and the predicate was wrong in the OTHER direction: `SENTENCE_BOUNDARY` requires the terminator to be followed IMMEDIATELY by whitespace, so an answer that quotes a record verbatim, closes the quotation with `."` or `.)` and starts its own next sentence has no answer-side boundary — and was reported as a substitution. Measured by a Phase 2 reviewer, four answers differing only in the character between the full stop and the space: plain stop silent, closing quote / closing paren / markdown bold all reported, on a quotation that substituted nothing. This module's own reference prose is full of `(SSRIs)` and `(M1)`. `mayEndASentence` says yes to a terminator anywhere in the gap, which is strictly more silencing and makes the recall-only property true.

**Both pooling legs are pinned on ASSEMBLED records, and the first draft of this paragraph said one of them could not be pinned at all.** `Reproductions.explained` (another cited record ended innocently at this answer position) and `carriedThrough` (some reproduction carries on past it) are both unreachable on the bundled sixteen-entry excerpt — the two records the injector produces for one question carry the same mechanism string, so they diverge together, and no record there states one passage twice. This decision then claimed `carriedThrough` was *"not constructible"*, and a reviewer constructed it in ten lines with ONE record stating a passage twice. Both shapes are ordinary in the data this runs on: a rendered reference record whose partner was PROMOTED is a `"; "`-joined list of per-partner items and DDInter partners routinely share a mechanism string. **Promoted is the qualifier issue [#355](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-chartsearchai/issues/355) added**: with nothing patient-specific to show the record normally carries names and severities rather than mechanism prose for this check to pool — normally, not always, since a rule carrying no token and no ATC has no name to shorten to and renders its paragraph anyway. So their cases build the record instead of injecting one, which is the right operand because this check is a pure function of an answer and a record's TEXT, and the cases beside them pin that it runs over production-rendered records on the real answer path.

**And the gap-predicate fix moved which leg the shipped data exercises.** Before it, the reference record's `"; "` item seam (`.); `) was not a sentence boundary, so a faithful full-mechanism quotation needed the FINDING record to explain it — the cross-record pooling. After it, the seam contains a `.` and the reference record explains its own continuation, so cross-record pooling stopped being reachable on that arrangement. The case that covers that answer still passes, but through the record-sentence exit rather than through pooling — it was named `aContinuationAnotherCitedRecordExplainsIsNotADivergence` and is now `aFaithfulFullMechanismQuotationIsNotReported`, named for the answer it protects rather than for a leg it does not pin.

**`MIN_REPRODUCED_WORDS` is twelve, and the suite decided the lower half of it.** The two live captures reproduce eighteen and nineteen words. At eight — the first draft's value — the check reports the module's OWN generated headline being restated: an answer saying *"Ciprofloxacin is in the same ATC class (J01MA) as the patient's active order"* against a record saying *"…as active order levofloxacin…"* reproduces nine words and then substitutes, which is structurally the same shape as the second capture. But that sentence is one this module composed about this patient and the prompt asks the model to carry, not knowledge-base prose whose wording is the evidence. `ClassCodeFidelityTest` is what pins it from BELOW, and no case was added there because it would only be a copy of that arrangement: its silence assertions capture the whole `org.openmrs.module.chartsearchai.api.impl` package, its canned answers restate that same generated headline, and on a floor of nine several of them redden with a failure message about class codes. **Which of them redden is deliberately not enumerated.** This decision published that count too, beside the constant's javadoc and a note in the test file itself, and the merge of #338 into this branch added cases to that file and falsified all three in one commit — the same defect as the site-count this decision withdraws above, made a second time in the same decision, and a count replacing a stale count is stale again on the next merge. Mutate the constant and read the failures. Nothing pinned it from above — raising it to thirteen left the whole api suite green, which silently disables a check whose only value is recall — so `aReproductionOfExactlyTheFloorIsStillReported` reproduces exactly twelve words and requires the report.

**What the WARN carries, and what it does not.** The patient, the record index, how many words were reproduced, and the record-side word offset. **No prose from either side.** A first draft logged a window of the record's own continuation on the reasoning that a reference record carries no patient data; that is false — a `safety_finding`'s detail embeds this patient's prescription display (`"… interacts with active order Warfarin 5mg"`) and a `drug_reference` record carries the ` Recorded for this patient: ` / ` Not recorded for this patient: ` / ` Matched in this patient's chart but not corroborated as a record of this drug: ` sections, whose clauses name this patient's allergens and conditions. Offsets identify the divergence without quoting it, which is the discipline `ClassCodeFidelityCheck` already states.

### Rejected alternatives

- **Render the mechanism verbatim in the answer — the ticket's own option 1, and it is NOT closed by this change.** Two readings. As a PROMPT instruction it cannot make the property hold by construction, which is the property the ticket says the architecture assumes; the module's own evidence is the model disobeying an instruction it already has (*"then the finding itself, carrying its own severity"*), `DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT` is a measured local optimum whose plausible edits have been measured and rejected before, and no api test can pin a paraphrase behaviour — the defect reproduces only against a long real chart. As DETERMINISTIC ASSEMBLY — the module emitting the verbatim mechanism into the answer — it WOULD hold by construction, and it is refused on different grounds: the clinician-facing text is the model's answer, #142 deliberately left every surfacing option open because each is a wire or UI change, and a silent edit of a clinical sentence is a larger decision than a check. Either way, **this check is the instrument that would measure such a change.** Nothing today detects paraphrase, so shipping a prompt edit beside it would make the A/B unreadable: an absence of `WARN`s would not separate "the prompt worked" from "the check is blind". The PR refs #337 rather than closing it.
- **Render LESS copyable prose** — cap what a `safety_finding` carries to its first sentence, which is #117's own remedy for this model garbling long verbatim copies. It shrinks the surface deterministically and is testable in the api suite, and it was not taken because the hazard clause is routinely in sentence two: in the ticket's first capture *"induce methemoglobinemia"* is inside the mechanism's opening sentence, but in the second, *"aminoglycoside antibiotics"* is what the answer excised from mid-sentence, and a first-sentence cap would have removed the rest of the paragraph from the prompt for every answer rather than only from the degraded ones. Worth re-proposing on evidence this check produces.
- **Report truncation as well as substitution.** An answer that stops reproducing and ends its sentence has stated nothing the record does not; reporting it fires on every answer that quotes one clause of a 150-word mechanism, which is most of them. That under-reports the ticket's weaker cousin — a hazard dropped by stopping early — and is the safe direction for a check whose failure mode is being ignored.
- **A rate published without a measurement.** Decision 35 shipped its analogue only after driving the production predicate over 340 captured live answers. The equivalent is measured below, by running the check IN PRODUCTION over the safety probe rather than re-expressing its predicate in a script.

### Measured

3.7.1 standalone, this branch's omod (lib-cache `.moduleLastModified` verified against the deployed file), bundled DDInter knowledge base, stock GPs, local Gemma E4B. `eval/drift-metric/capture_probe_safety.sh` default matrix — 4 patients x 5 drugs — plus one warm-up query: **21 live answers**, of which **7 cite a reference-group record at all**. The check reported **5 divergences across 4 of those 7**, and no `ClassCodeFidelityCheck` line in the same window.

Every one of the four was read against the chip the answer was reproducing. All four are real degradations of the cited record's own text, and three delete clinical content:

| cell | reproduced | what the answer did to the record's words |
|---|---|---|
| joshua / aspirin | 18, then 12 | dropped *"the vasodilator and hypotensive effects of ACE inhibitors"* and *"myocardial infarction"*, stitching two record sentences into one |
| mary / erythromycin | 22 | *"simvastatin and **lovastatin** and **their** active acid metabolites"* became *"simvastatin and **its** active acid metabolites"* — a drug name deleted; *"isoenzyme"* became *"isozyme"* |
| mary / clarithromycin | 14 | *"significantly"* became *"signficantly"* and *"acid"* became *"acd"* inside a recited Major mechanism |
| agnes / warfarin | 12 | *"Aspirin, **even even** in small doses"* — the issue's own third observation, the text re-emitted token by token rather than copied |

**Zero false positives in this sample**, and the sample reproduces #337 on a different patient set and different drugs from the two captures in the issue.

**Re-measured on the merging head** (the same probe, after this branch merged `main`): 7 of the 20 default cells cite a reference-group record, 5 divergences across 4 of those 7, no `ClassCodeFidelityCheck` line in the same window, and the same four cells with the same corruptions. **Read the table as a record of one capture and not as an invariant, because the counts are phrasing-sensitive**: a hand-typed *"can she take clarithromycin?"* on that patient reported 12 words continuing at word 17, byte-reproducible across three runs, where the probe's own phrasing of the same cell reported 14 continuing at 19. That is greedy decode's known sensitivity to the question's wording, not drift in the check. It says nothing about the rate on charts unlike these; the probe is 4 patients. Three of the seven citing answers were NOT reported, and this measurement does not establish whether any of them should have been — the probe capture keeps the answer and the chips, not the cited record's own text, so a missed divergence there is not readable from it. The residue this check accepts is recall, by construction of every exit above; measuring it needs a capture that keeps the records.

### What it costs on the request path

Measured by a Phase 2 reviewer with a throwaway JUnit case driving the real `reportUnfaithfulReferenceProse` over records from the real `injectedSafetyFindingChart`, 40 warm-up plus 40 timed calls per arrangement: **705 µs** on a realistic chart (2 records / 2619 chars, 300-word answer quoting the finding) and **1.2 ms** at ADR Decision 57's largest measured cell (6 records / 5178 chars). `ClassCodeFidelityCheck` is 41 µs on the same arrangement — a different cost class, since that one is a regex pass over characters and this is a dynamic program over the product of two word counts.

The product is of two quantities this module has explicitly declined to bound: `MAX_INTERACTION_RENDER_CHARS` caps one record and Decision 57 refuses to cap the record count. A synthetic 20-record chart with a 3000-word answer reaches 54–79 ms. That is above anything the 504-cell sweep behind Decision 57 produced, and no remedy is taken here: a per-call vocabulary filter (skip the dynamic program where the record has no `MIN_REPRODUCED_WORDS` consecutive words in the answer's word set) was implemented and measured at 1.2 ms for that synthetic cell and ~0.4 ms on a realistic one, and declined — a filter that is wrong silences the check, which is the fail-closed direction, and 0.4 ms does not buy that risk. Available later on evidence this check produces.

The answer is tokenised only after at least one cited reference record has been found, so a stock install — where `chartsearchai.drugReference.enabled` is false and no answer cites reference prose — pays a map build and nothing else.

### What this cannot see

- **A hardcode of the reference-group pair inside this check's own gate.** The gate asks `ChartSearchAiUtils.referenceGroup` rather than a type name, so a reference type added later is covered without this class changing. Nothing guards that, and — unlike `isGroundingDemoteOnly` and `referenceSlice`, whose blindness a third type did close — a third type did **not** close this one: issue #354 added `drug_class_note` and re-measured, and the inline pair still ships green, because no case drives a record of that type through this check. What would close it is such a case, not another type. Said rather than left to be inferred.
- **A gap read as a sentence end.** An abbreviation dot, and under `mayEndASentence` any terminator at all, reads as one. Both bit-driven conditions are SILENCING, so it can only add silence — on the record side the "reproduced a sentence and moved on" exit, on the answer side the "stopped copying" one. A misread boundary therefore costs a report and never causes one. That argument rests on two things and neither is decoration: the predicate must be the weak one (above), and the boundary bit must NOT be part of word equality — were it, a record writing `"(e.g. chloroquine"` against an answer writing `"(e.g., chloroquine"` would break the reproduction and then report two IDENTICAL words as a substitution.
- **A divergence inside the clauses `renderFinding` appends.** The record-sentence exit covers the SEAM, not the clause's interior: a reproduction running from the detail into the clause, or one inside the thirteen words of `STRENGTH_CAUTION`, is reported. Excluding it means teaching this check where a finding's own prose ends, which is `renderFinding`'s knowledge and would be a second copy of it. The first draft of this change proposed exactly that accessor and deleted it.
- **A substitution inside a reproduction shorter than twelve words**, wherever it sits. Issue [#338](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-chartsearchai/issues/338)'s own captured answer is an instance: a repeated class code earlier in the same sentence leaves the substitution after it in a run of seven words, so this check is silent on it — measured at [Decision 59](#re-measured-after-337-the-check-that-landed-since-is-silent-on-this-issues-own-capture), which also records why a report from this check is not evidence that a drug name was mangled.
- **Which cited record a WARN names when two of them diverge at one answer position.** The first in citation order wins, and nothing pins that — mutating it to last-wins leaves the whole api suite green. It decides both handles the line gives a maintainer, since the line quotes no prose, and it is named here so a reader does not infer from a green suite that it was chosen. **It was a tie-break with no correctness content while this check was log-only, and [Decision 74](#decision-74-a-divergence-the-prose-check-finds-is-stated-on-the-response-not-only-in-the-log) changed that**: `Reproductions.diverged` keeps the FIRST divergence at an answer position, so where two cited records diverge at the same word the second is dropped — and that index is now one a client is shown, or rather is not. Measured on that change: two records sharing a fourteen-word prefix and diverging at one answer word produce one WARN and one published index. Collecting the statement from every divergence rather than from the position-deduped map would close it and would also change what the WARNs report, so it is recorded rather than taken.
- **That a digit is a word character.** `Words.of` takes runs of letters AND digits, so `CYP450 3A4` and `5-HT1A` segment the way the record writes them; narrowing it to letters alone leaves the suite green. Nothing in the bundled arrangements turns on it.
- **An elision the model marked with three ASCII dots.** The same cut written `…`, `—` or `[…]` IS reported — correctly, since issue #337's second capture is an elision and dropping *"aminoglycoside antibiotics"* out of a sentence a clinician reads is the defect whatever marks the cut — but `...` puts a terminator in the gap, which the weak gap question reads as the answer ending its sentence. So which elisions are seen depends on the glyph the model chose. Closing it means a gap question that is not silencing, and then a quotation closed with `."` is a false report again; the two cannot both be had.
- **Its own failure — and since [Decision 74](#decision-74-a-divergence-the-prose-check-finds-is-stated-on-the-response-not-only-in-the-log) this branch decides a WIRE value rather than only a log line, though no path is known to reach it either way.** Mutating its `return null` to an empty list leaves the whole build green, so nothing stops a later edit publishing "the check ran and named none" for a run that measured nothing. The `catch (RuntimeException)` is defence in depth and no test reaches it: every reference-group mapping's text is read earlier in the same method by `ChartSearchAiUtils.referenceSlice`, which has no guard of its own, so a record that throws on read never gets as far as this check. That is a latent gap in `referenceSlice`, reported here and not fixed.
## Decision 62: The chip publishes the rating it was ordered on, verbatim, and says what a client may not conclude from it

**Status: Accepted** (August 2026) — implemented, issue [#340](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-chartsearchai/issues/340). Additive to the wire; raises, suppresses and rewords no chip.

### Context

`ChartSearchAiRestController.serializeSafetyWarnings` wrote three keys — `type`, `drug`, `detail` — and `SafetyWarning.getSeverity()` stopped there. That value is public, populated by every rated arm, and is what `PAIR_SEVERITY_DESCENDING` and `SCREENED_PAIR_SEVERITY_DESCENDING` order the two PAIRWISE arms' chips by before `maxPairChips` cuts the list — at the time of writing the drug-in-play arm emitted in its entry's own rule order and sorted on nothing, which was a property of that arm and not of this field; issue #346 has since ordered it too, on the finding rather than on this value alone. The module goes to real lengths to get the pairwise ordering right and then discarded the key at the last step. #340 measures the consequence on a 3.7.1 standalone: five chips — two Major, one Minor, two contraindications — indistinguishable on the wire except by substring-matching the rendered English inside `detail`.

This is recorded in this repo as a fault rather than as a decision. #207 exposed the field for the api-side ordering assertions and scoped itself to that ("Not serialized onto the REST response"); nothing anywhere states a reason for withholding it. What does exist is a reader that had to parse the prose: `eval/drift-metric/score_probe_safety.py`'s `CHIP_SEVERITY` regex, whose own comment calls the parse *"the fault issue #207 exists to have removed"*.

**It is a different question from #283 and does not reopen it.** How strongly a finding licenses a clinical call — `licensesWithholding`, `STRENGTH_WITHHOLD` / `STRENGTH_CAUTION` — stays prompt-facing, on Decision 37's stated ground that a clinician-facing chip is not where this module gets to assert what a rating licenses. Severity is the SOURCE dataset's rating, and on the bundled dataset it is already quoted verbatim to the clinician inside `detail`; publishing it asserts nothing that prose does not. (On an operator `json` dataset the prose need not carry it at all — which is the argument for the field rather than against it, and is scoped in "The prose is not a fallback" below.)

### Decision

`serializeSafetyWarnings` writes a fourth key, `severity`, carrying `SafetyWarning.getSeverity()` **verbatim and unnormalized**, `null` where the finding carries no rating. The key is unconditionally present, for the reason `groundedForWire` gives about its own field: a key a client can read without first asking whether it is there. All three emission sites — the blocking `/search` response and the SSE `done` and `grounded` events — go through that one helper, so one edit covers them.

**Verbatim, and not coerced into a closed vocabulary.** `DrugSafetyValidator.severityRank` trims, case-folds, and maps every unrecognised value — including `null` — to the same answer, *unrated*: exempt from `clearsSeverityFloor`, sorted above `Major` by `severityPriority`, and licensing withholding in `ratingLicensesWithholding`. Run rather than read, by driving those three predicates directly on `"Severe"`, `""` and `null`: all three inputs answer identically on all three predicates — priority `2147483647` against `Major`'s `3`, withholding true, floor cleared — while `"  major  "` and `"MAJOR"` both rank as `Major`, which is the trim-and-case-fold half. Publishing `null` for a value the module does not recognise would therefore hide a rating the chip's own prose still quotes, which re-creates the field-versus-prose contradiction the ticket exists to remove. So the field says exactly what the dataset wrote, and the documentation says what may not be concluded from it: there are **three** classes on the wire, not two — a rating the module recognises, `null` meaning the rule carries no rating, and any other string a dataset supplied — so `severity != null` does not mean "the source rated this", a client must trim and case-fold as `severityRank` does, and an unrecognised value is *unrated*, not a floor.

**The closure answer #340 asks for.** `type` is closed: every production construction site passes a `SafetyWarning.TYPE_*` constant, so a client may switch on it — with a default branch, because that is a property of the arms rather than of the wire format. `severity` is **not** closed: `DrugReference.Interaction.severity` is a plain Jackson-bound string with no vocabulary check and no `DrugReferenceValidity` rule over it. Measured 2026-08-30 through the real `DdiDrugReferenceSource.load()` and `DrugReference.Interaction#getSeverity()`, never a re-expression of them — over the shipped KB's **590,312 interaction links** across 2283 entries the distinct values are exactly `Major` (101,962), `Moderate` (378,830), `Minor` (24,690) and `Unknown` (84,830), with none null and none blank; over the bundled curated seed, all five of its INTERACTION rules are null (its contraindication rules carry no severity field at all). Unit: interaction LINKS as `getInteractions()` publishes them, each unordered row appearing on both partners' entries.

**The prose is not a fallback — and the reason is not the one this decision first gave.** The first draft said a rated rule with no mechanism text names its rating nowhere in its sentence. Measured through the real `DdiDrugReferenceSource.load()` over the shipped KB, that is false for `sourceFormat=ddinter`: `noteFor` writes a note for every row — `severity + ". " + mechanism`, or `severity + " severity interaction (… no mechanism description on file)."` where the row has none — so of its **590,312** links, **0** carry a null note, **0** a blank one, **0** are rated with no note, and **0** have a note that does not start with its own severity word. On the shipped dataset the parse works on every link.

What it rests on there is only that `detail` is prose this module rewords freely and holds out as no contract — and the drift-metric scorer's own comment records a reword walking straight past its parse. Where the parse breaks outright is `sourceFormat=json`, whose note and severity are independently authored fields: a rule may carry no note, in which case `interactionWarning` (which appends one only when the rule carries it) leaves the rating out of the sentence entirely, or carry one whose leading word is a different rating. `ChartSearchAiSafetyWarningSeverityWireTest.theRatingIsPublishedEvenWhereTheProseNamesItNowhere` drives both.

**This supersedes the wire shape recorded in Decision 23's "Wire & frontend" section** — and is itself superseded, for the chip's own shape, by Decision 70, which adds a fifth key (`chartOrderBridges`) — (`{ type, drug, detail }`, and two emission surfaces where there are now three) and the count in Decision 51's trade-offs ("writes three named keys"). Both are left as the dated records of what was true then and marked inline where they stand, per this file's own convention for a superseded mid-body paragraph; this is where the current shape is stated.

### Alternatives considered

- **Normalize to a closed set — publish one of four recognised words, else `null`.** Rejected: the module would then deny a rating its own chip prose quotes, which is the defect being fixed, one level along. The vocabulary is the dataset's and the module has never enforced one.
- **Trim the value before publishing.** Rejected for the same coherence reason in the corner it exists for: `DdiDrugReferenceSource` takes `row.get(2).asText()` untrimmed, so a padded rating would appear padded in both the field and the note, and trimming one of them would make them disagree. The documentation states the client-side rule instead.
- **Leave the wire alone and document the prose parse as the supported reading**, which #340 offers as the alternative if publishing is not wanted. Rejected: it makes a clinician-facing sentence a contract, and this repo already has one reader boxed in by that — the drift-metric scorer, whose comment records a reword walking straight past it.
- **Publishing a derived discriminator beside the verbatim value** — a `rated` boolean, or a canonical rank off `severityRank`. Raised in review of this change, and the argument for it is real: telling every client to trim, case-fold and treat an unrecognised value as unrated asks each of them to reimplement `severityRank` in its own language, which is the cross-language duplication this repo refuses elsewhere, and #201 removed a field rather than leave clients a value they had to interpret. Not taken here, and not because it is wrong. It is a second published field with a contract of its own — what a canonical rank says about a value the module does not recognise, and whether a normalized *rank* stays on the right side of #283 — so it is a decision on its own evidence rather than a rider on this one, which #340 did not ask for. And the residue it would close is bounded: the shipped dataset emits only the four canonical spellings, so the interpretation rules bite only on operator-authored data. Left open rather than refused.
- **Teach `score_probe_safety.py` to prefer the new field.** Not taken, and the scorer's own comment already argued why before this change existed: every capture and fixture in that tree predates the field, so a wire-based read would be inert on all of them and the parse must stay regardless. Its comment was edited but its behaviour was not — the now-false factual claim replaced by the measurement above, and the pointer re-aimed at the field for a future capture.

### Effect

Four keys instead of three on every chip, on all three emission surfaces. Nothing else about a chip moves: `type`, `drug` and `detail` are byte-identical, no chip is raised or suppressed, and the ordering and cap are untouched. With the drug-reference feature off — the shipped default — the array is still empty and nothing changes at all.

`ChartSearchAiSafetyWarningSeverityWireTest` pins it at all three emission sites. Since Decision 60 those sites reach the serializer through `putSafetyChips`, so a single `map.put` governs all three and deleting it reddens every case in the class at once. To see a site on its own, make that site's `putSafetyChips(...)` call write an empty chip list: each SSE site then isolates to the single case written for it, while the blocking site is read by every case that calls `searchChips()` and so reddens more than one. Mutate and read the failures rather than expecting a count. It also pins on the SERIALIZED bytes of the SSE `done` event that an unrated chip's key survives as JSON `null` rather than being dropped — a claim the blocking path cannot make, since Spring serializes its `Map` after the test can look. Its fixture carries the three shapes the reporter's own capture does not: a rated rule with no mechanism note, a rating the module does not recognise, and a chip whose sentence and rating disagree. The last of those is there because it was needed — a serializer that parses the prose and falls back to the field agrees with the field wherever the two agree, so it survived the class until that chip existed. Mutate the serializer and read the failures rather than trusting this paragraph.

### Trade-offs

- **+** A client can prioritise, filter, colour or collapse by severity without depending on wording this module does not treat as a contract.
- **+** The rating a chip was ordered on is now observable at the surface the ordering exists for.
- **−** A field whose vocabulary the module does not control is now published. That is the honest shape — it is the dataset's rating — but it moves a burden onto the client, and the README carries the three rules that go with it rather than leaving them to be discovered.
- **−** The reference frontend (`openmrs-esm-chartsearchai`) does not read the field, so nothing renders differently until it does. This is the wire contract's half only, exactly as Decision 23's `group` discriminator was.
- **−** `everyPublicZeroArgumentAccessorOfAWarningNamesAKeyOnTheWire` introduces a NEW contract on `SafetyWarning` — every accessor a client can read names a wire key — which this class did not previously state and, for this very field, contradicted. Adding a public zero-argument accessor now means publishing it or arguing the exception. That is the intended cost: a value the module computes, orders chips by, and then drops at serialization is the shape of this defect, and it survived from #207 to #340 with nothing failing. What the guard does **not** reach is stated on the guard itself, and is not restated here — the list has grown once already.

## Decision 63: One response names one active order one way, so the reconciliation stops being the fold's

**Status: Accepted** (August 2026) — implemented, issue [#339](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-chartsearchai/issues/339).

### Context

#339 reports one `/search` response naming the patient's active orders by two conventions at once. Measured on the 3.7.1 standalone at `09717dc7` over the bundled DDInter knowledge base, one payload with subject `Hydrocortisone` carried `active order celecoxib` / `diclofenac` / `ibuprofen` beside `active order Dexamethasone` / `Prednisone` / `Budesonide` / `Methylprednisolone`; and the Ibuprofen × Diclofenac pair read `active order Diclofenac` for `"Can I give her ibuprofen?"` and `active order diclofenac` for `"Please screen her current medications"`. It quotes this repo's own record of the non-cosmetic form — one payload holding `active order Isoniazid / Rifapentine` beside `active order isoniazid` — and states the invariant a reader relies on: *"the invariant currently held is 'one chip never contradicts itself', not 'one response names one order one way'"*.

The cause is where the question was asked, not what it answered. `reconciledPartnerName` (Decision 39's `foldedPartnerLabel`) had exactly ONE call site, inside `addInteractionWarnings`' `classRelationships(...).entrySet()` loop. Every other rule chip took the two-arg `interactionWarning`, which hardcodes `partnerLabel` — the knowledge base's own match token, which the `ddinter` parser lower-cases from the partner row's RxNorm generic. So which name an order got was decided by whether the class arm happened to have a sentence to fold onto that chip: the NSAID partners share no subgroup and no curated group with hydrocortisone, and the corticosteroids share `H02AB`. The same fact explains the second shape — the drug-in-play arm can fold and `addActiveOrderPairInteractions` cannot, `classRelationships` running per in-play substance while a screening question names none.

### Decision

Ask the same reconciliation at every rule chip in both active-order arms, through one entry point (`reconciledPartnerFor`). One gate and not two — but the gate itself moved twice under review, and the first two rounds of this decision said it did not. See **What the widening cost the gate** below; a false "the gate is untouched" is what the next change reads instead of re-measuring.

The partner is found from `SubjectRule.partner` — the entry `activeOrderEntryFor` already resolved, the module's one answer to "which partner is this rule about" — looked up in a per-pass index on `CoMedications` keyed on **two** substance keys — the ladder's `OrderPartner.labelEntry` substance, and every key in `OrderPartner.substances` — with a **third**, non-substance rung added in review round 2 and described in the trade-offs below. The second is not decoration. A partly-covered combination order is named after ONE of the substances it contains (`soleSubstanceOf` resolves the covered code), so a rule about the other half resolves an entry whose substance key is not the partner's; keyed on `labelEntry` alone the index misses it and that chip goes on printing `isoniazid` beside the other's `Isoniazid / Rifapentine`. Measured: removing the `substances` pass reprints **Decision 39's** live payload — `active order isoniazid` beside `active order Isoniazid / Rifapentine` — and `OneOrderNameAcrossOneResponseTest.twoRulesAboutOneCombinationPrescriptionNameItOnce` is the one case that reddens. (Not the hydrocortisone payload the Measured section above quotes: that one is reached by the `labelEntry` pass, and `theTicketsOwnArrangementOverTheShippedKnowledgeBaseNamesOneWay` stays green under this mutation.)

**The chip names its partner by the row THIS RESPONSE names that substance by, not by the ladder's own label.** The ladder elects its row with `canonicalRow` alone (`entryForAtcCode`), while every other name slot in a response is elected by `interactionSubject` — the row the patient's own record claims most strongly, then `canonicalRow` among the rows tied on that (#194). Promoting the ladder's answer to every rule chip without that step reproduces #187 at a new site: measured through the real `validate` over `ddi-substance-identity.json`, a charted `Pfizer-BioNTech Covid-19 Vaccine` order was named `Tozinameran (…)` — a row of the same substance the chart does not record — while the screening arm named that same prescription by the charted row, so one substance was named two ways in one response. `reconciledPartnerName` therefore asks `SubstanceSubjects.subjectOf` first and **gates on the elected row**, since the gate must prove the token names the row whose display is about to be printed. `addPartnersForUnmappedOrders` already elects its own rung's row this way (#228); this is that rule reaching the code rung. Pinned by `OneOrderNameAcrossOneResponseTest.aPartnerIsNamedByTheRowThisResponseNamesItsSubstanceBy`; reading `partner.labelEntry` instead reddens it **and `aClassOnlyChipNamesAPartnerByTheSameRowARuleChipDoes`**, the cross-arm case review round 1 added below (re-measured at review round 11's head). **No claim is made about what that mutation leaves green.** One stood here — "leaves the rest of the api suite green" — from the round this paragraph was written; it went stale inside the branch the moment round 1's case arrived, survived round 10's sweep of the neighbouring claims, and would have told a maintainer that the second failure was collateral rather than the cross-arm invariant this decision exists to establish. Mutate the election and read the failures.

**And the CLASS arm elects the same way, or the migration is half done** (review round 1). Its own sentence — a class-only chip's, and the class half of a folded chip whose arms did not reconcile — still took `OrderPartner.label`, which on the entry rung is `canonicalRow`'s display. So the two elections disagreed on exactly the multi-row substance above, and one response named one prescription two ways again — now in two visibly different strings rather than the case difference the ticket opens with, which is the form it calls the non-cosmetic one. Measured through the real `validate` over the SHIPPED knowledge base, a chart carrying one `Methylprednisolone (topical)` order asked about prednisolone and warfarin: `Prednisolone is in the same ATC class (H02AB) as active order Methylprednisolone` beside `Warfarin interacts with active order Methylprednisolone (topical)`, which `renderFinding` copies verbatim into the prompt as two co-medications. `DrugSafetyValidator.classPartnerName` is that election applied to the class arm's own sentence. It moves ONLY the ENTRY rung: a label an ORDER supplied has no row to elect, and a bare code or `[ATC …]` is the absence of a name that Decisions 38 and 39 refuse to let an entry name displace, so both keep `OrderPartner.label` untouched. Both conjuncts discriminate — mutate each and read the failures, all three mutations re-measured at review round 11's head. Dropping `labelEntry != null` dereferences null inside `SubstanceSubjects.subjectOf` on the CODE-ONLY shape (both fields null), so what reddens is an NPE thrown from a chip-naming site and its failures are NOT confined to cases about naming a partner. **No count is published for that one, deliberately**: this decision published one, and round 10 measured it wrong by 5×, most of the failures sitting in a class about answer-versus-class-code fidelity — so a maintainer following the instruction above could not tell the surplus from damage they had just done, which is the whole reason the instruction is to read the failures. Dropping `namingOrder == null` reddens cases in `PartialOrderCoveragePartnerTest`, `UnmappedOrderClassPartnerTest`, `DuplicateTherapySelfChipTest` and this decision's own `OneOrderNameAcrossOneResponseTest` — the class list is the load-bearing part of that one, since two of those classes are pre-existing. Reading `OrderPartner.label` outright reddens `OneOrderNameAcrossOneResponseTest.aClassOnlyChipNamesAPartnerByTheSameRowARuleChipDoes` (re-measured at review round 11's head; no claim is made about the rest of the suite, for the reason the paragraph above gives). **`PartialOrderCoveragePartnerTest.theMergedPartnerIsNotNamedAfterHalfOfACombination` is the pre-existing case that states the rule review rounds 5 and 6 broke** — it survived them because its arrangement raises no refusal, which is why round 7's own cases are stated over the class SENTENCE and not only over the label. That case is driven over `ddi-class-only-and-rule-one-partner.json`, a verbatim shipped-KB slice of the arrangement above: the prednisolone pair's only KB rule is rated `Unknown`, which the shipped `minInteractionSeverity` default filters, so it reaches the class arm alone, while warfarin shares no subgroup and reaches the rule arm alone.

The injected `drug_reference` note moves with the chip, through the mechanism Decision 51 already built (`SafetyWarning.reconciledPartnerNoteName`). Moving one and not the other is #292 one surface along.

`unambiguouslyNames`' rival-claimant collection stops being a `getAll()` walk. It was affordable while it ran once per FOLDED chip — *"the rare outcome of the class arm rather than the ordinary one"*, as its own javadoc said — and asking it once per rule chip makes the asks grow with the drugs in play, which `CoMedicationResolutionPerPassTest.theCoMedicationResolutionDoesNotGrowWithTheDrugsInPlay` forbids. **A memo over the asks cannot restore that**: the distinct (token, entry) pairs a pass reconciles are 3 at one drug in play and 7 at two over that fixture's own order list, so de-duplicating the repeats leaves the difference growing. The dataset is inverted ONCE per pass instead — `DrugReferenceService.nameIndex()` over `DrugReference.nameKeys()`, read back through `entriesNamedBy` — because one walk is one walk however many chips read it. Measured by mutating the loop back to a `getAll()` walk and reading that case's failure rather than by reading a counter: it reddens at two drugs in play, 27 sweeps against the flat 20 the pass costs at one. (An earlier draft of this paragraph recorded 19, which is below the flat figure and so could not have been the with-the-walk number; mutate and read the message rather than trusting either.)

### What the widening cost the gate

Asking one gate at many more call sites did not leave the gate alone, and each round of review found one more way it did not. Both corrections NARROW what the widened sites would otherwise print, which is why the "no new mis-attribution class" claim survives while "the gate is untouched" does not.

**The ENTRY rung asks the gate of the row the RESPONSE elects, and falls back to the ladder's own** (review rounds 1 and 3). Round 1 moved the operand from `OrderPartner.labelEntry` to `SubstanceSubjects.subjectOf(labelEntry)`, because printing `canonicalRow`'s pick at a chip-naming site is #187 and the class arm elects with `interactionSubject` everywhere else. That moved WHICH ROW `unambiguouslyNames` is asked about, and the two rows of one substance can answer differently — CLAUDE.md's rule is that the gate is asked of the row about to be PRINTED, and a row's own claim is not its substance's. Measured through the real `validate` over `ddi-fold-tied-token.json`, itself a verbatim shipped-KB slice: a charted `Atropine (ophthalmic)` order mapped to `S01FA01` elects that presentation, whose claim on the token `atropine` merely ties `Hyoscyamine`'s, while `canonicalRow`'s `Atropine` claims it outright. Round 1 therefore turned a permit into a refusal, the rule sentence fell back to `partnerLabel` while `classPartnerName` kept the elected row, and ONE folded detail read `active order atropine` beside `active order Atropine (ophthalmic)` — one prescription, two names, where `09717dc7` printed `Atropine` in both. Strictly worse than the base on that arrangement, and measured by mutating the operand back.

Round 3's answer is that the printed row is the FIRST of (the response's elected row, the ladder's own row) that the gate admits. Both are rows of one substance, the gate is still asked of the row that is then printed, and nothing is printed on a sibling's claim — so `aRuleTokenTheLaddersRowOnlyTiesKeepsItsOwnToken` stands: on the unmapped-order rung the two rows COINCIDE and there is no second ask to make. The order is a preference between two rows the gate may each admit, never a widening of it, and it is monotone over the base: where the election is refused it restores exactly what `09717dc7` printed. `FoldedChipOnePartnerNameTest.aRowTheResponseElectsButTheTokenDoesNotClaimFallsBackToTheLaddersOwn` is the pin; dropping the fallback reddens it and `noFoldedChipNamesOneActiveOrderTwoWays` in that same class — `Tests run: 1683, Failures: 2`, re-measured at review round 10's head — and nothing else in the api suite. The second is not a second pin of the fallback: that sweep took this arrangement as its TENTH run, and without the fallback the chip still folds but names the one order `atropine` AND `Atropine (ophthalmic)`, so what fails there is its one-name assertion and not its count.

What it does NOT close, stated as a residue this change LEAVES rather than as one it inherits: a class-ONLY chip in the same response still names that prescription by the elected row, because `classPartnerName` has no rule and so no token for any gate to read. Measured over the shipped knowledge base on that same one-order chart, asked about every `S01FA` substance at once: the three rule chips read `active order Atropine` and the two class-only ones (Tropicamide, Cyclopentolate (ophthalmic)) read `active order Atropine (ophthalmic)`. At the merge base `abb36813` — and at `09717dc7` before it, re-checked at this head by reading `OrderPartner.label` at `classPartnerName`, which is what the base did and which makes the class-only chips say `Atropine` too — all five read `Atropine`, so on THIS arrangement the response still carries two names where the merge base carried one, i.e. this is a REGRESSION against the merge base and not only an unclosed inheritance — a divergence of ROW between two real dataset names, where HEAD before this round had a divergence of row AND case with a lower-cased token on one side. Closing it means either printing a row the gate refused, or making a class-only chip follow a reconciliation decided per RULE — and two rules about one partner can carry different tokens and so reach different answers, which is #136's shape one level along. Nothing pins it, and the ticket's own measured sweep (100 → 94 divergent responses) is where the population is. It needs the order's display to carry the route parenthetical the knowledge base's row uses; with an ordinary display (`Atropine 1% eye drops`) this head is consistent and better than the merge base, and review round 4's own one-order sweep over every named row of the shipped KB (1839 charts, class-sibling questions, both heads) reported divergent responses 1253 → 24 and case-only divergences 1110 → 0 with **3** responses moving from a case-only difference to a substantive one — **a regression on those three**. Those three figures are review round 4's measurement and were NOT re-measured here; what was re-measured at this head is the `Atropine (ophthalmic)` arrangement above, both sides. To reproduce the sweep: for each named row of `DdiDrugReferenceSource.load()`, one active order displaying that row's name with its own ATC codes, a question naming two substances sharing its level-4 subgroup, through the real `validate`, flagging any response in which two `active order <label>` strings for one prescription differ.

**REVERTED in review round 7 — kept because the reasoning is the record of why. See the round-7 paragraph below.** **The ORDER rung refuses where the naming order's display also names a substance THIS RESPONSE raises chips about** (review round 3, narrowed to a response-level question in review round 4, `CoMedications.displayNamesAnotherChipSubject`). `namesNamingOrder` asks only that the rule's token name the prescription's display; a fixed-dose combination's display names BOTH constituents, so where a subject of the response is one and the partner the other it is satisfied and the chip reads as a drug interacting with itself, the interacting agent gone from the lead and left only in the mechanism prose. That is the shape `DdiDrugReferenceSource`'s own parse-time self-pair guard keeps out for a different cause, and `renderFinding` copies the chip into the prompt verbatim as a citable `safety_finding` carrying `STRENGTH_WITHHOLD`. **The trade-off bullet below used to call this fixture-only, and that was wrong**: measured through the real `validate` over `DrugReferenceTestSupport.shippedEntries()`, one active order displayed `Lisinopril / Hydrochlorothiazide` with codes `{C09BA03, C03AA03}` — the first uncovered, so `soleSubstanceOf` resolves the second and `nameByOrder` renames the partner — asked *"Can I give her lisinopril?"* printed `Lisinopril interacts with active order Lisinopril / Hydrochlorothiazide — Moderate`, where `09717dc7` printed `active order hydrochlorothiazide`. Fixed-dose combinations are ordinary prescriptions and this knowledge base rules on the constituents of several.

**Superseded by review round 7, which removed the conjunct entirely.** **Round 3 asked the conjunct of the CHIP's own subject, and that was itself an instance of the ticket's defect** (review round 4). `reconciledPartnerName` took `subject` as an operand, so two rule chips about ONE prescription carrying the SAME rule token got different answers: the chip whose subject the display happens to name fell back to `partnerLabel` while the other printed the display. Measured at this head over `DrugReferenceTestSupport.shippedEntries()`, the same one-order `Lisinopril / Hydrochlorothiazide` chart asked *"Can I give her lisinopril and amiodarone?"* printed `Lisinopril interacts with active order hydrochlorothiazide` beside `Amiodarone interacts with active order Lisinopril / Hydrochlorothiazide` — one prescription, two names, where the merge base `abb36813` printed `hydrochlorothiazide` in both. So round 3 fixed one chip and broke the response.
