Salicylates may interfere with the renal elimination of methotrexate…"*, byte-identical ×2 — **and it DROPS finding `[366]` (Celecoxib × Prednisone) from the eight-order cell in both runs**, narrowing its own claim to *"interactions … between Ibuprofen and the patient's current medications"*, which is false of the pair it dropped. §3c was unharmed. Dropping a finding is the regression this section names, so the prompt edit was reverted and the candidate redeployed. Residue 1 above is therefore a known-cost trade rather than an open question: the arm that closes it is the arm that loses a finding, and closing it wants a shape neither arm tried.

**What CI can hold, and what it cannot.** A prompt regression is invisible to the build, so the prompt assertions are the whole of the automated defence — and they are CONTENT assertions, not existence ones, since a sentence that names the class and then refuses satisfies the naming half: `SafetyVerdictSeverityGradationTest.assertCurrentMedicationBranch` requires each branch to open by NAMING the medication, to carry the prohibition on opening by refusing to give a drug, to contain no `"No"`, and to contain no PERMISSION lead IN ITS SIBLING'S OWN WORDS — a permission worded away from those is held by the seal below and not by this helper — with the single-property mutation that holds each recorded beside it — asked of EVERY sentence that names a class and says how to open, not the first, so a second sentence instructing a refusal for the same class is caught rather than skipped. Beside it, `.theTwoCurrentMedicationBranchesAreExactlyTheseWords` seals both branch sentences verbatim, for the reason the permission-term paragraph below gives. Two further cases cover what a per-branch check cannot: `.aSetMixingAProposalCallAndACurrentMedicationCallIsLedByTheStrongest` reads the ranking sentence POSITIONALLY (withholding call, then change-of-therapy call, then the caution), because naming both classes is satisfied by a sentence that inverts them; and `.everyRefusalInstructionInTheParagraphIsGatedOnTheWithholdingClause` requires every sentence carrying the `"No"` token to be gated on the clause that licenses a refusal or to be the paragraph's own prohibition on one, which is the only one of the three that reaches a refusal instruction naming no class at all. Each of those was measured by the mutation it reddens, on `026613de`. That is a guard over TEXT, so what it cannot see is what the model then produces, which is what the A/B above measured.

**The permission term is round 3 of this PR's hardening, and until it this paragraph and CLAUDE.md both overclaimed.** They said the helper held both directions; it held the refusal one. A fresh reviewer measured three single-hunk prompt mutations that give a current-medication branch a permission lead while keeping every other property — the caution-current branch reworded to *"open by naming that the drug can be given and the caution in the same sentence"* (the direction `STRENGTH_CAUTION_CURRENT_MEDICATION`'s own javadoc names), the same branch harmonised with its proposal sibling, and the WITHHOLDING-class branch given *"stating that it can be given"* — and all three were green across the whole api module. That is the fail-open direction: the *Both classes* paragraph above is entirely about it, and #107 arm C measured a presence-shaped permission inverting the call 5 of 6 times — and in the third mutation's case it is instructed for a Major screened pair of the patient's own prescriptions, #348's own two-order reproduction cell. So the half was HELD rather than the claim narrowed, and the phrase is read OFF the proposal-caution branch's own lead instead of copied — that sibling is required to lead with a permission, so harmonisation is the failure mode, and a sibling reworded away from one fails in the derivation rather than leaving the assertion vacuous. What it cannot see, and what round 4 then did about it: a permission worded away from the sibling's words (*"may be continued"*) passed all four properties — measured on the pushed head, once on the caution-current branch and once on the withholding-class one, both green across the whole api module. Round 4 closed that by SEALING both branch sentences verbatim (`.theTwoCurrentMedicationBranchesAreExactlyTheseWords`), on the reasoning that any legitimate reword re-opens the A/B this section records, so a guard that fires on every reword is a tripwire telling the next maintainer a live measurement is owed — the same argument `DrugClassQuestionNoteTest.theRenderedNoteIsExactlyTheseWords` rests on. The four properties stay beside it: a seal says nothing about which part of the sentence mattered. What neither reaches, because both select sentences the same way, is a permission instructed in a sentence that names no class core or says nothing about opening. Within a branch sentence it is not scoped to the LEAD, so a permission stated later in the same sentence reddens it too. In the same round `.theEvidenceAgainstClaimIsConditionalOnTheStrengthTheFindingStates` was widened from the FIRST occurrence of the evidence-against claim to every non-negated one, having been green on the change branch rewritten as the pre-#348 refusal without the `"No"` literal.
## Decision 73: A condition rule's bare-containment match is corroborated by a word boundary, not by a resolution

**Status: Accepted** (September 2026) — implemented, issue [#309](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-chartsearchai/issues/309). Discharges the residue [Decision 42](#decision-42-a-recorded-clause-needs-corroboration-not-just-a-match) states in its last trade-off bullet and [Decision 44](#decision-44-a-finding-says-how-its-rule-reached-the-chart) repeats. Prompt-facing only: one leg added to `corroboratedByTheChart`, no chip, no wire field, no matcher changed — which is also the LIMIT of the fix, the clinician-facing chip still asserting the condition on the ticket's own reproduction; the trade-offs carry it.

### Context

Decision 42 made the injected record ask whether anything CORROBORATES a contraindication rule's match before stating the clause as the chart's own reading, and scoped that to a self-named ALLERGY rule. `DrugSafetyValidator.corroboratedByTheChart` therefore answered `true` unconditionally for every other rule, so a CONDITION rule reached `Recorded for this patient:` on the strength of `PatientClinicalContext.hasConditionToken` alone — which is bare containment, deliberately, because a curated condition token is meant to match a fragment.

Both decisions recorded the reason the scope was defensible, and it is a real one: the two corroborating legs resolve a drug NAME (`aMatchedRecordNamesTheEntry` through `matchesDrugName`, `allergicSubstanceKeys` through the allergen arm's identity question) and no arm resolves a recorded condition to a reference substance. #309 filed the deferral so it had a home, and asked for a measurement before any remedy.

### The measurement

Run over the OpenMRS 3.7.1 reference-application demo dictionary through the real predicates. `PatientClinicalContext.containsToken` is the canonical home for the figures, both corpora and what each is a count OF, beside #223's and #141's for the allergy list; what follows quotes only the few this decision turns on.

What it decided, in three findings. **The hazard is real and clinical**: `liver` matches 30 of that dictionary's 2581 condition candidates and 20 carry it only inside a deliver/delivery form; `deficiency` 14/7, all immunodeficiencies; `psoriasis` 4/2, one of them a different disease. A hepatic or renal contraindication is the most ordinary curated condition rule there is.

**The ticket's own hypothesised remedy does not work in the FILTERING form it proposed** — "a condition token too short or too generic to be safe as a containment match". No threshold over the token separates safe from unsafe: hazardous tokens occur at 35 distinct character lengths spanning 1 to 46 and at every word count from 1 to 6, and the longest nests inside its own negation (`traumatic intracranial subarachnoid hemorrhage` inside `Nontraumatic intracranial subarachnoid hemorrhage`). Hazard is a property of the (token, recorded value) PAIR and the loader holds no condition corpus. A REPORTED loader finding keyed on length is still defensible — a single-word token of one to three characters is hazardous 61-100% of the time on both corpora — and was declined for a different reason, below.

**The ticket's premise about corroboration is true of the legs and does not settle the question.** What redeems a condition match is not a resolution but a BOUNDARY: whether the token reached the record as a word of it.

### Decision

**A matched CONDITION rule's clause is stated as the chart's own reading only where some recorded condition it matched carries the token as a WHOLE WORD.** `DrugSafetyValidator.aMatchedConditionCarriesTheToken`, the third leg of `corroboratedByTheChart`, reading witnesses from the new `PatientClinicalContext.conditionsMatching` — the condition list's counterpart of `allergensMatching`, sharing `containsToken`'s own primitives through one extracted scan so the witnesses and the boolean cannot drift. Where it fails the clause goes to Decision 42's third section, which asserts no contraindication and denies none, and since Decision 44 the `safety_finding` beside it states the same provenance.

**`DrugReference.containsWord` and deliberately not `matchesOrderName`.** The condition haystack is prose in the clinician's own wording, which is the shape `containsToken` describes it by, so it takes the PROSE rule — the accessor `CLAUDE.md` names for that operand shape. The order-name rule's two-letter tail allowance is measured over drug names, and choosing it here would be a caller picking an allowance of its own, which is #260's shape.

**Read through the witness accessor, for symmetry with the allergy leg and NOT because it answers differently from scanning the whole condition list.** It does not, and the first draft of this decision claimed it did: `containsWord` is strictly stronger than the containment the witnesses are filtered by, so a condition carrying the token as a word is already a witness. Measured by mutation — swapping the loop to `context.getConditionTokens()` reddens nothing. It is recorded because the allergy leg's per-witness form IS load-bearing (`matchesDrugName` can accept a record `hasAllergyToken` did not match), so the symmetry invites the reader to assume the same here. What the witness form buys is a question this leg cannot yet ask — WHICH recorded condition redeemed the match — and a boundary rule weaker than containment, where the filter would begin to matter.

**The MATCH is untouched, and the reason is fail-open rather than #223's fragment case.** `hasConditionToken` and `containsToken` are byte-identical, and every chip this arm raises is unchanged. Tightening the match would DROP chips rather than hedge them, and it drops them on the free-text shape the condition list is really about: `containsWord("GI bleeding", "gi bleed")` is false, so the shipped seed's own gastrointestinal-bleeding rule would stop firing for a condition a clinician typed. That is the argument. The one #223 supplies for the allergy list is its class token — `containsWord("NSAIDs", "nsaid")` is false too — and it does not transfer to conditions, the shipped seed's four condition tokens naming findings rather than a class. **An earlier draft of this paragraph rested on `peptic ulcer` inside `history of peptic ulcer disease`, and that is refuted rather than merely weak**: `containsWord` ACCEPTS it, so it is not a case tightening would cost anything. Deleted here and at its other homes on 2026-09-03; do not reinstate it.

**The three legs are not interchangeable and none is asked of the other's rule type.** #309 forbids widening `selfNamedAllergyRule` to conditions in as many words, because `ref.isNamed(token)` asks whether the token is one of the DRUG's names, which is meaningless for a condition token. This is not that widening: it asks a question about the RECORD, not about the entry.

**The loader rule was declined rather than shipped beside this.** It warns where this fixes, it is silent on five of the six witnesses recorded on `containsToken` (all but `gi` are five characters or more), and it is silent by construction on every shipped dataset. It remains available if an operator population ever justifies it; the derived threshold is recorded on `containsToken` so it need not be re-measured.

### Trade-offs

- **+** The record no longer states as this patient's chart's own reading a condition clause that reached the chart by a mid-word accident, and it says so where a model reads it rather than falling silent.
- **+** Zero cost over the two measured corpora — **and the base that zero is over is one token, not four** — its matches counted per corpus and never summed into a total, the recorded concepts being a subset of the candidate ones. Per token (measured 2026-09-03 through `hasConditionToken` and `aMatchedConditionCarriesTheToken`): `peptic ulcer` matches 5 of the 2581 candidate values and 1 of the 704 recorded ones, all as whole words; `gi bleed`, `severe hepatic` and `renal impairment` match **nothing** in either corpus, so "all four tokens match every value they match as whole words" is vacuously true for three of them and neither corpus says anything about what the boundary rule does to those three. State it with its base wherever it is published (#243) — the unbounded form had reached every document that carries this claim before it was measured. That is the proxy #223 used for the allergy side, run for conditions — with the same weakness, three of these tokens being as unmeasured against a coded corpus as an operator's own file is. The bound is load-bearing — both corpora are CODED concept names; see below for what free text costs. The token set the claim is ABOUT is pinned by `ConditionRuleBoundaryCorroborationTest.theShippedSeedPublishesExactlyTheFourConditionTokensTheMeasurementWasOver`, so a fifth rule prompts a re-measure rather than a re-wording.
- **+/−** No matcher moves, so #223's declined tightening is not reopened from another direction, and the arm's chips are byte-identical **on the wire**. The `SafetyWarning`'s own `uncorroboratedChartMatch` flag does flip for a condition rule, which is exactly what the injected finding reads — and it has no path to a client: its accessor is package-private to `...chartsearchai.reference`, `ChartSearchAiRestController.serializeSafetyWarnings` sits in another package and names each chip's keys one by one rather than reading the warning reflectively, and it is not a field of `SafetyWarning.ChartOrderBridge`, whose own fields ARE read reflectively (Decision 70). So no field a client reads moves, and no contraindication chip's collapse key reads it either. **Read that serializer for the key set it writes rather than any list here** — an enumeration of it stood in this bullet and was stale on the day it was written, #347 having already added a key it did not name, and the residue tracked below is closed by changing that very method. **Read the next bullet before citing this one as reassurance**: on the hazard case the surviving chip is the false claim, not a preserved safety net.
- **−** **Only the model-facing half of the defect is fixed. The clinician-facing chip still asserts the condition, unqualified.** For the ticket's own reproduction — a patient whose one recorded condition is `Status Post Cesarean Delivery`, asked `Can I give her naltrexone?` — the injected record and the `safety_finding` now hedge, and `/search` `safetyWarnings` still carries exactly one chip, reading `Naltrexone is contraindicated by an active condition: acute hepatitis or liver failure`. Measured 2026-09-03 by driving `DrugSafetyValidator.validate` over `chartsearchai-test/drug-reference-condition-token-nesting.json`. That surface has no third section to hedge into, so a clinician reads a categorical about a chart recording a caesarean delivery while the model reads a hedge — the two surfaces now disagree about one chart, in the direction the ticket was filed about. Not closed here, for two reasons: tightening `hasConditionToken` is the wrong remedy (fail-open — it drops the `GI bleeding` chip, see **The MATCH is untouched** above), and the chip's own wording is measured prose that `DrugSafetyChipLabelTest` and #108 constrain, so a hedged or demoted condition chip is a change on its own evidence. The allergy side's analogous demotion exists (`contraindicationRank`, #223) and is allergy-typed; extending it to conditions is one shape a follow-up could take. **Tracked as [#374](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-chartsearchai/issues/374)**, which carries this reproduction and the three candidate remedies, so the residue has a home rather than living only in this bullet — which is the reason #309 itself was filed. **A live defect this decision documents rather than fixes, and not a residue the design accepts** — every other mention of the surviving chip in this decision, in `README.md` and in `ConditionRuleBoundaryCorroborationTest` cites it as reassurance for the cases the boundary rule OVER-hedges, which it is, and on the hazard case it is this instead.
- **−** **A clinically right prefix or suffix compound is hedged.** `Lymphedema` IS oedema and `Osteoarthritis of knee` IS arthritis; a rule on `edema` or `arthritis` matching only those is sent to the uncorroborated section. Measured: `edema` 13/7, `carcinoma` 8/2, `arthritis` 10/3, `cerebral` 10/2, `ulcer` 21/2 over the candidate corpus. Hedged rather than dropped — the section asserts nothing and denies nothing — and pinned as a case rather than described, `ConditionRuleBoundaryCorroborationTest.aClinicallyRightCompoundIsHedgedToo`, so a future change reads the cost. Closing it needs morphology, which is a different decision on different evidence.
- **−** **The free-text half is unmeasured on both sides, and it is where the rule does cost — including on the shipped seed's own tokens.** The demo database's `condition_non_coded` column holds one placeholder string across all 853 rows, so a condition recorded in the clinician's own wording — the shape the fragment rationale is really about — is outside both corpora. Reasoned from the rule rather than counted, and pinned as a case: a condition typed `GI bleeding` is hedged against the seed's `gi bleed`, and `peptic ulceration` against `peptic ulcer`. Those are INFLECTIONS, the commonest free-text shape and one neither corpus can exhibit; neither of the module's two allowances reaches them — 0 letters for prose and 2 for an order name, against tails of three and five — and picking a third at a call site is what #260 forbids, so what would actually close this is morphology rather than a wider tail. `ConditionRuleBoundaryCorroborationTest.anInflectionOfAShippedTokenIsHedged` pins the first of them, with the seed's other condition rule — which still states as recorded — as its control; the second is stated and not pinned. The `en` locale bound is the same shape of gap; #141 records that a francophone deployment reads different strings for the same concepts.
- **−** **The section's and the finding's WORDS were written for the allergy case and are reused for this one.** For a self-named allergy rule the token IS one of the drug's names, so "not corroborated as a record of this drug" is the question actually asked. For a condition rule the module never asks whether the token names a drug — its uncertainty is only about the wording of the matched condition — so the sentence names a corroboration it never attempted. Taken deliberately rather than missed: prompt wording here is measured rather than argued, Decision 42 already records this lead's own exact wording as unmeasured, and a second unmeasured sentence in citable evidence is the larger risk. Nothing false about the PATIENT is asserted either way, and the section still asserts nothing and denies nothing. A wording change is visible — `InjectedContraindicationCorroborationTest.theThreeSectionLeadsAreTheWordsAModelReads` pins the literal — so this is a trade to revisit with a measurement, not a latent defect.
- **−** **It reaches an ALLERGY rule's clause too, wherever one entry files both under a single note.** "Condition-only" describes which rule the leg is asked of, not the blast radius: `addContraindications` resolves the reading over clause TEXT as well as over keys, so a condition rule that now hedges no longer clears an identically-worded allergy clause of another key. Neuter the leg and read the failures. Most are condition cases; the ones that carry this argument turn on an ALLERGY rule's clause — `InjectedContraindicationCorroborationTest.aClauseAnotherRuleOfTheSameEntryDoesRecordIsStatedAsRecorded`, `UncorroboratedFindingProvenanceTest.aClauseAnotherKeyOfThisEntryStatesAsRecordedIsNotHedged` and `.theWordsTheFindingPrintsAreNotHedgedWhereAnotherKeyStatesThemAsRecorded`, whose Levoketoconazole arrangement prints the `levo` allergy rule's note and has its hedge cleared by a condition rule of another key. Read the failure list rather than this one: an earlier wording named two and the mutation produces three, which is the shape that makes a surplus look like damage the reader just did. Correct behaviour, and the second stage doing what Decision 44 built it for; recorded because the scoping sentence reads narrower than the change is.
- **−** **A condition rule whose clause is right for a reason no boundary can see is now hedged.** Both allergy legs can already miss a real allergy (Decision 42's ketoconazole case); this leg can miss a real condition the same way. That is why the section's lead states what the module established rather than a categorical about the chart, and why the finding's call does not move.

## Decision 74: A divergence the prose check finds is stated on the response, not only in the log

**Issue [#337](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-chartsearchai/issues/337), second round.** [Decision 61](#decision-61-prose-the-answer-reproduces-from-a-cited-reference-record-must-be-reproduced-faithfully) gave the module an instrument for the defect and shipped it report-only. It works: measured on that issue's own re-run against `main` @ `77c0f9a2`, `ReferenceProseFidelityCheck` named live divergences on a second patient set — an answer that reproduced a cited record and returned DDInter's `naproxen` as `naproxenic`, and another that came back with `hypoprothrombinemice`, `metabolizm` and `hipercoagulability` inside prose it was otherwise copying verbatim. The issue stayed open on one sentence: *"what remains open is that the prose still reaches the clinician unchanged."*

**The gap this closes is not the paraphrase; it is that the finding was invisible to everyone but a maintainer reading a log.** A degraded safety sentence reached the clinician carrying a citation marker, and every observable field of the response read exactly as a faithful answer's would — so nothing a `/search` consumer could render said the marker's own record reads otherwise. That is the failure [Decision 67](#decision-67-a-question-naming-a-drug-class-is-told-so-rather-than-resolved-to-members-the-classification-cannot-honestly-supply) answered for the drug-class note, [Decision 60](#decision-60-a-bounded-pairwise-interaction-list-states-its-own-bounds-on-the-response) for the interaction extent and [Decision 64](#decision-64-a-finding-states-which-of-this-patients-own-orders-each-substance-it-names-was-resolved-from) for the chart-order bridges, each with the same remedy: the module states what it did, on a key, rather than depending on the wording of a generated answer.

### The decision

`ReferenceProseFidelityCheck.reportUnfaithfulReferenceProse` returns the **distinct citation indexes it warned about**, in report order. `LlmInferenceService` captures that at the call site the check already had, on both answer paths, and carries it on `ChartAnswer.getUnfaithfullyRenderedCitations()`; `ChartSearchAiRestController.putModuleStatements` publishes it as `unfaithfullyRenderedCitations`, so it reaches `/search`, `done` and the trailing `grounded` event through the one composition point. The check's reporting is untouched — every sentence of Decision 61 about what it reports, and about what it cannot see, still holds.

**What travels is the CITATION and never a word of either text**, and that is the part of this change that was designed rather than chosen. The obvious richer key — the record's own sentence, so a client could show what the record actually says — requires cutting a sentence out of the record, and the only per-word boundary information this check has is `ChartSearchAiUtils.mayEndASentence`, whose javadoc forbids exactly that use (*"It must not be used to SPLIT a text into units: `Q12H. `-shaped prose and an abbreviation dot both answer yes here"*). Publishing a clipped fragment as *what the record says* would be this issue's own defect committed by its fix. (The module does HAVE a splitter — `SENTENCE_BOUNDARY` — and the next sentence is why reaching for it is not the answer either.) Splitting with `SENTENCE_BOUNDARY` instead is not a free swap either: the divergence POSITION is decided by the weak predicate, so the published unit would not be the unit the check reasoned about — two spellings of one question inside one method, which is the shape [#260](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-chartsearchai/issues/260) records the cost of. Three further reasons fell out once the prose was dropped, and each is independent: Decision 61 records that a divergence inside the clauses `renderFinding` appends IS reported, so the published sentence could be `STRENGTH_WITHHOLD` boilerplate or the chart-order clause's items, which are this patient's own prescription displays; a `drug_reference` record's text carries the ` Recorded for this patient: ` sections naming her allergens and conditions, and appears on no wire key today; and for a `safety_finding` the chip's `detail` already publishes the record's MECHANISM half, which is the part a richer key would mostly have re-sent. **That last one is a strict subset, and the README states the gap rather than implying a join**: the record also carries its `Safety finding — <drug>: ` prefix and the clauses `renderFinding` appends, and a `safety_finding`'s `resourceUuid` names the SUBJECT drug alone — measured by driving the real injector, one drug screened against two active orders produces two records, two citation indexes, one `resourceUuid`, and two chips sharing one `(type, drug)`. The chips carrying that pair are a candidate SET and nothing on the response picks one out. A client can flag the rendering; it cannot be handed the correction.

**One record is one entry.** The divergences arrive keyed on ANSWER position, so a record the answer diverged from twice contributes two — and the issue's own comment records exactly that shape live, two WARNs on record `[253]` from one answer. The WARNs stay per divergence, because a maintainer needs both offsets; the statement is of the citation, because what a client can act on is *this citation's rendering is not the record's words*, once.

**`null` and an empty list are different statements, and the empty one says less than it looks.** Null is the absence of a measurement: the check failed, or an answer path did not run it. Empty is a measurement of none — but it also covers the answer citing no readable reference record at all, which on a stock install is EVERY answer, `chartsearchai.drugReference.enabled` being `false`. So an empty list never means *the answer was compared against its records and found faithful*, and the README says so rather than leaving a client to infer a certificate from a silence that the check's own recall limits already forbid.

**It is stated as `null` on the early `done`, and that is the documented ordering rather than a gap.** The check runs after `searchStreaming` hands the ungrounded answer to its consumer — deliberately, under the comment that reserves that boundary for the user-visible response — so the early answer genuinely has no measurement to state. `interactionPairs` behaves the same way for the same class of reason, and `unresolvedDrugClass` does not, being known before the model is called. Moving the check ahead of the handoff was considered and refused: it would put a word-level dynamic program (~0.7 ms typical, 54–79 ms on the synthetic 20-record chart Decision 61 measured) in front of the event a user waits on, to deliver a statement that is not needed to render the answer.

**The copy at the serializer is a correctness requirement, not caution.** The accessor returns a `Collections.unmodifiableList` wrapper in every non-null case, the empty one included — the constructor wraps a fresh `ArrayList`, so `Collections$EmptyList` never arises from it and the `UnmodifiableRandomAccessList` is what does the damage. XStreamMarshaller — the converter openmrs-core selects for `Accept: application/xml` — refuses both wrappers, which turned every chip-carrying XML response into a 500 in [#347](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-chartsearchai/issues/347). Unlike `chartOrderBridges()` this accessor can also return null, so the copy is guarded rather than unconditional: `new ArrayList<>(null)` throws.

### Rejected alternatives

- **Rewrite the answer's degraded sentence from the record.** Decision 61 refuses the edit on its own grounds — the clinician-facing text is the model's, and a silent edit of a clinical sentence is a larger decision than a check — and there is a second reason of this change's own. The check detects the divergence POINT and does not know where the degraded span ENDS; replacing to the end of the answer's sentence would delete whatever the model legitimately added inside it, trading an omission risk for a fabrication risk in clinical text. Available later on evidence this key produces.
- **A prompt instruction to quote the mechanism verbatim.** Decision 61 records why: it cannot make the property hold by construction, `DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT` is a measured local optimum whose plausible edits have been measured and rejected, and no api test can pin a paraphrase behaviour. Unchanged by this.
- **A per-citation field on `references[]`, beside `grounded` / `source` / `withheldInteractions`.** It puts the statement on the object the statement is about, and `serializeReferences` is already one implementation for all four surfaces. It was declined because the early `references` SSE event is emitted before the check runs, so the field would be null on the event whose whole purpose is early rendering, and a client would have to read the same field twice and prefer the later one. A top-level key that is null on the early terminal event and populated on the trailing one is the shape this module already documents for `interactionPairs`.
- **An audit column beside the wire key.** [Decision 57](#decision-57-the-injected-reference-slice-gets-a-durable-observable-and-deliberately-no-cap) set the precedent for a measurement carried on the `ChartAnswer` AND written to the audit row, and this check is described throughout as the instrument that would measure whether a later fix worked — which a wire-only statement leaves to log-grep. It is not taken because the two statements this one is modelled on, `unresolvedDrugClass` and `interactionPairs`, reach no audit column either, and adding one here alone would make the audit table's coverage of this module's statements arbitrary rather than complete. Worth taking for all three together, on evidence that someone wants the prevalence.
- **Publishing the class-code check's answer at the same time.** `ClassCodeFidelityCheck` stays report-only ([Decision 35](#decision-35-a-class-code-in-the-answer-must-come-from-a-record-the-answer-cites) point 4). The asymmetry is recorded rather than left to be read as an oversight: #337 asked for the prose one, the same shape is available for the other, and nothing here establishes a clinician-facing use for an edited ATC token that Decision 35 did not already leave open on #142.

### What this does not do

**It does not close #337.** The answer's prose is still degraded; the module states that it is. A clinician reads a frontend, and rendering this key is a change in `openmrs-esm-chartsearchai` — the same split this repository already records for the other half of [#201](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-chartsearchai/issues/201). The PR refs the issue rather than closing it.

**And it inherits every limit of the check it publishes.** Decision 61's "What this cannot see" is unchanged and is now, for the first time, a limit on something a client renders: an elision written with three ASCII dots, a divergence inside a reproduction shorter than twelve words, a gap read as a sentence end. **More than one changes CHARACTER rather than merely audience, and Decision 61 has been amended at each.** Where two cited records diverge at one answer position the second is dropped — a tie-break between two handles in a log line, now a citation index a client is not shown. And the check's own failure branch, defence in depth while nothing read it, now decides a published value; nothing pins that either, and no path is known to deliver it to a client, the line it guards being re-read where a throw errors the request instead. That is the argument for the README's second prohibition — an absent entry is not a certificate — and it is why publishing the measurement is worth more than publishing a per-answer verdict this check could not honestly make.
